## CSS Selector {#selector}
`*`   selects all elements
`div`  selects all <div> elements
`div, p`  selects all <div> and <p> elements
`div p`  selects all <p> within <div>
`div > p`  selects all <p> one level deep in <div>
`div + p`  selects all <p> immediately after a <div>
`div ~ p`  selects all <p> preceded by a <div>
`.classname`  selects all elements with the attribute class="classname".
`.c1.c2`  selects all elements with both c1 and c2 within its class attribute.
`.c1 .c2`  selects all elements with class c2 that is a descendant of an element with class c1.
`#idname`  selects all elements with the attribute id="idname".

E.g. Internet Explorer and Chrome may render the same web page differently. ::: ::: ## 📋 Web Standard ::: {.f2} * There are 3 major groups that govern the standard for the Web: * World Wide Web Consortium (**W3C**) formed in 1994 maintains the [CSS specifications](https://www.w3.org/Style/CSS/) * Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group (**WHATWG**) formed in 2004 and is the publisher of the [HTML and DOM standards](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/) * **TC39 technical committee** of [Ecma International](http://www.ecma-international.org/publications/standards/Standard.htm), renamed from European Computer Manufacturers Association (ECMA) in 1994, maintains the standards for JS * These groups consist of Mozilla, Apple, Google, Microsoft and other invited members. ::: ##
